content: Neomycin is an antibiotic that is prescribed to prevent or treat bacterial skin infections. It is not effective against infections caused by fungi or viruses. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses, so you should consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Neomycin is available in cream and ointment forms, which are applied directly to the skin. Typically, it is used one to three times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before applying neomycin, clean the affected area thoroughly and allow it to dry. Then, gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it disappears. Use only enough medication to cover the affected area. After applying the medication, wash your hands. Avoid applying neomycin to a child’s diaper area, especially if the skin is raw, unless specifically instructed by a doctor. If directed to use it in this area, do not use tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as these can increase the absorption of the drug and lead to harmful effects. Apply only small amounts of neomycin to scrapes, cuts, burns, sores, or wounds, and do not use it more frequently than directed. Neomycin can be absorbed into the body through broken skin, potentially causing kidney problems and hearing difficulties. Before using neomycin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to neomycin or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins. Let your doctor know if you have or have ever had kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using neomycin, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget to apply a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Neomycin may cause side effects. If you experience irritation, burning, redness, rash, itching, hearing difficulty, or decreased urination, contact your doctor immediately. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store neomycin in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Neomycin may become discolored, but this does not affect its effectiveness. Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly, and consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Neomycin is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms of infection persist after completing the course of neomycin, contact your doctor.
